description: Somos Tesh Sonus, estudiantes de Ingeniería de Sistemas Informáticos que participan virtualmente en NASA Space Apps 2026 (Carmen City). Nuestras fortalezas: desarrollo web y Python. Nos apasionan las herramientas de código abierto que convierten los datos abiertos de la NASA en experiencias accesibles y multisensoriales. Para el reto Earth Information Jukebox, buscamos compañeros con habilidades en audio web, visualización de datos, comunicación científica en inglés y diseño gráfico.
summary: TerraFonia · SONUS (The Earth Information Machine) is an interactive web observatory that translates NASA Earth science telemetry into dynamic, real-time spatial sonification. Centered around SONUS—a procedural 3D crystalline core with audio-reactive GLSL shaders—the system streams planetary observations across an interactive 3D Earth globe. A custom Web Audio engine deterministically converts atmospheric and environmental datasets into sound: MERRA-2 2m temperature modulates carrier pitch, specific humidity shapes harmonic timbre, wind velocity vectors (𝑢10𝑚, 𝑣10𝑚) drive spatialized stereo turbulence, FIRMS/VIIRS active fires trigger stochastic percussive crackles, and MODIS cloud fraction controls low-pass resonant filtering. Featuring 5 real planetary presets (Amazon Basin, Arctic Cryosphere, Sahara Desert, Equatorial Pacific, and a Missing Data sensor validation test), plus real-time FFT spectrum visualization and an assistive voice copilot, TerraFonia offers an intuitive, accessible acoustic window into our living planet.
details:
TerraFonia · SONUS — The Earth Information Machine converts complex, multidimensional NASA Earth observation data into verifiable acoustic signals, transforming silent satellite telemetry into an intuitive scientific listening experience.

Interactive Cyber HUD & 3D Core:

A dual-column telemetry console renders an interactive 3D WebGL Earth globe alongside the SONUS Crystalline Core—a real-time procedural sphere engineered with dynamic Fresnel refraction shaders and particle emissions that pulsate in direct response to synthesized sound waves. A live FFT audio analyzer provides immediate waveform and frequency feedback.

Deterministic Scientific Sonification Engine:

Rather than arbitrary sound effects, every acoustic parameter maps directly to peer-reviewed NASA Earth science variables using the native Web Audio API:

NASA MERRA-2 Atmospheric Reanalysis: 2-meter air temperature governs the fundamental oscillator frequency (110 Hz − 440 Hz); specific humidity modulates FM harmonic brightness; eastward and northward 10-meter wind vectors drive filtered pink noise and stereo binaural panning.

NASA MODIS / VIIRS (FIRMS): Active fire counts and thermal anomalies inject stochastic rhythmic crackles and tension.

NASA MODIS Terra: Vegetation indices (NDVI) introduce organic harmonic overtones, while cloud fraction modulates low-pass resonance filters (300 Hz −8000 Hz).

Planetary Presets & Data Integrity:

Users can explore 5 distinct planetary systems: Amazon Basin (Biotic Pulse), Arctic Ocean (Cryospheric Winds), Sahara Desert (Thermal Convection), Equatorial Pacific (Trade Winds), and a dedicated Missing Data Quality Orbit, which demonstrates strict scientific error handling by representing missing sensor data honestly (null values) without synthetic interpolation.

Accessibility & AI Copilot:

TerraFonia incorporates an interactive voice copilot (powered by the Web Speech API) providing auditory explanations of regional climate dynamics, ensuring multi-sensory accessibility for blind and low-vision researchers, educators, and students.

Architecture & Technologies:

Built with Vite, React, TypeScript, Three.js, GLSL Shaders, and the native Web Audio API. Automated CI/CD deploys the instrument directly to GitHub Pages.
